section_1_goal_and_primary_metric.goal: To demonstrate that a native XML query processing system should support query plans that mix tree-based navigation and structural joins (based on inverted lists) to achieve better performance.

concrete_numbers.meaning: For Query 2 on the 100K document, the hybrid plan (ZZ -> UN) took 17.2ms, while the pure navigational plan (UN) took 18471.1ms.
For Query 2 on the 100K document, the hybrid plan (ZZ -> UN) took 17.2ms, while the pure structural join plan (ZZ) took 425.3ms.
For Query 3 on the 100K document, the hybrid plan (UN -> ZZ) took 57.7ms, while the pure navigational plan (UN) took 9308.3ms.

section_2_comparison_baseline.why_this_is_the_right_comparison: The paper's central argument is that systems using either only tree navigation or only inverted list filtering are suboptimal, which was the common approach in the literature at the time.
section_2_comparison_baseline.limiting_design_assumption: A single query processing paradigm, either purely tree-based navigation or purely index-based structural joins, is sufficient and optimal for all XML path queries.
pointers: [quote: '...there has been a sharp line demarcating the use of inverted list filtering and tree navigation.']
[quote: '...building systems that keep the two kinds of processing separate is suboptimal...']

specific_tools_or_algorithms: Cost models for navigational (Unnest) and index-based (ZigZag Join) operators
section_3_primary_mechanism_tooling_clas.what_is_being_optimized: The sequence of navigational and index-based operators in a query plan for an XML path expression.
section_3_primary_mechanism_tooling_clas.state_or_ir: A path expression query, which is broken into prefixes and suffixes during optimization.
section_3_primary_mechanism_tooling_clas.output: A query plan that may mix navigational and index-based operators.

section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.summary: Introduced a unified query execution engine that can compose operators from two different processing paradigms: tree-based navigation (Unnest) and index-based structural joins (ZigZag Join).
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.baseline_assumption: Query plans are homogeneous, consisting of operators from only one processing paradigm (either navigational or index-based).
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.why_baseline_did_not_include_it: The two processing paradigms were developed and used separately in the literature, and integrating them requires a common data addressing scheme and mechanisms to convert between operator data formats.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.mechanism_level_implementation: The system provides two operator types: Unnest (navigational) and ZigZag Join (index-based). It also provides mechanisms for converting data between the formats required by each operator (XKeys for Unnest, postings for ZigZag Join), allowing them to be chained together in a single plan.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.tradeoffs_or_costs: Increased system complexity and a runtime cost for converting between data formats (e.g., XKey to posting lookups).

section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.summary: Developed a cost-based optimizer using dynamic programming to select the most efficient hybrid plan from the space of possible operator combinations.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.baseline_assumption: Query optimization is confined to a single processing paradigm. There is no mechanism to choose between paradigms for different parts of a query.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.why_baseline_did_not_include_it: The need for such an optimizer only arises once hybrid plans are possible. Without the ability to mix operators, there is no choice to be made between them.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.mechanism_level_implementation: The system uses recursive cost formulas for the Unnest and ZigZag Join operators, which depend on data statistics. A dynamic programming algorithm populates cost matrices to find the minimum cost plan for evaluating a given path expression by considering all valid ways to split the path between the two operator types.
section_4_key_deltas_vs_baseline.tradeoffs_or_costs: Requires collecting and maintaining detailed statistics about the XML data, some of which are novel (Skip Factor, Skip Count) and potentially expensive to compute. The optimization process itself adds overhead.

principles.name: Composability
principles.mechanism_trigger: The ability to pipe results between the Unnest (navigational) and ZigZag Join (index-based) operators within a single query plan.
principles.why_it_applies: The central idea is to compose operators from two distinct processing paradigms. The system explicitly provides mechanisms to convert between formats to enable this composition.
principles.pointer: [quote: '...a native XML repository needs to support query plans that utilize these query processing approaches, and needs to be able to pipe intermediate results between the two.']

principles.name: Modularity
principles.mechanism_trigger: The system architecture is split into a Data Manager for navigational access and an Index Manager for inverted lists.
principles.why_it_applies: The system is built from two distinct modules, each responsible for one of the processing paradigms. The mixed-mode execution composes these modules.

rejected_or_borderline_principles.name: Generalized Design
rejected_or_borderline_principles.reason_rejected_or_borderline: The system does not create a single, more general operator. Instead, it composes two specialized, distinct operators. Composability is more specific.

principles.name: Cost-based
principles.mechanism_trigger: The dynamic programming algorithm that uses cost formulas based on data statistics to select the best plan among the hybrid alternatives.
principles.why_it_applies: The paper explicitly develops and validates a cost model to guide the choice of query plan, which is the definition of cost-based optimization.

principles.name: Equivalence-based
principles.mechanism_trigger: The optimizer's search strategy, which considers different ways to partition a path expression across Unnest and ZigZag Join operators. All generated plans are semantically equivalent.
principles.why_it_applies: The optimizer explores a search space of different, but semantically equivalent, plans to find the one with the lowest cost. For example, /A/B/D can be evaluated as a single Unnest, or as a ZigZag join for /A/B followed by another operation for /D.

principles.name: Workload-Aware
principles.mechanism_trigger: The cost model's reliance on statistics that capture the specific structure and cardinality of the XML documents being queried.
principles.why_it_applies: The choice of the optimal plan is not fixed but depends on the properties of the data (e.g., element cardinalities, path selectivities), which are a proxy for the workload. The experiments show that the best plan changes for different queries and data.

section_7_compound_equation.equation: Homogeneous Query Plans + Co + Ep + Cm -> Mixed-Mode Query Plans

principle_composition_rationale.why_these_principles_work_together: The system first uses Composability (Co) to create a new, larger space of possible query plans by allowing operators from different paradigms to be combined. This expanded space of semantically equivalent plans is the domain for an Equivalence-based (Ep) optimizer. Finally, a Cost-based (Cm) model is required to effectively search this space and select the plan with the best performance, as the optimal choice is data-dependent.

what_each_principle_contributes.contribution_to_equation: Enables the creation of hybrid query plans by allowing navigational and index-based operators to be chained together.
Provides the decision-making framework to select the best plan from the available hybrid options based on estimated execution cost.
Defines the search space for the optimizer, which consists of many semantically equivalent plans constructed from different combinations of operators.

principle_composition_rationale.transfer_question: In what other domains could composing specialized, heterogeneous execution engines and using a cost-based optimizer to select among them outperform a single, general-purpose engine?

section_8_physical_properties_summary.concrete_number: Up to 1072x speedup for some queries

best_candidate_new_principle.name: None
best_candidate_new_principle.why_existing_principles_are_insufficient: Existing principles sufficiently cover the paper's mechanisms. The combination of Composability (Co), Equivalence-based (Ep), and Cost-based (Cm) planning accurately describes the classic database optimization pattern of expanding the plan space and then using a cost model to choose the best option. This paper applies that pattern to a new combination of execution strategies (navigational and index-based).

section_11_normalized_summary.one_sentence_mechanism: Enables and cost-optimizes hybrid query plans that compose navigational tree-traversal operators with index-based structural join operators to accelerate XML path queries.
specific_tools_or_algorithms: Cost models for navigational (Unnest) and index-based (ZigZag Join) operators
